title: Two-qubit binegativity can increase under local amplitude damping
authors: Xiao-Lan Zong, Wei Song, Ming Yang
abstract: It has been conjectured that the binegativity of two-qubit states is an entanglement monotone. We present a full-rank state as a counterexample: applying amplitude damping to only one of the qubits can increase the binegativity of the state. The output state remains full rank, and the amount of increase can be calculated exactly. In addition, we construct a family of counterexamples that vary continuously with a parameter. In the corresponding one-way local operations and classical communication protocol, the probability-weighted average of the binegativity over the branches after the local measurement is also higher than that of the initial state.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that the binegativity of two-qubit states is not an entanglement monotone under local operations. By constructing specific counterexamples involving local amplitude damping and local measurements, the authors demonstrate that the measure can increase, challenging current conjectures about entanglement preservation under realistic noise models.
main_problem: The paper challenges the conjecture that binegativity, a measure of entanglement, is an entanglement monotone under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) or Positive-Partial-Transpose-Preserving (PPT) channels.
main_result: The authors provide counterexamples showing that applying local amplitude damping or performing local measurements can increase the binegativity of two-qubit states, thus violating the expected monotonicity.
method: The analysis involves constructing specific full-rank two-qubit states and applying known quantum channels, such as local amplitude damping, to calculate the change in binegativity.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-qubit quantum states ($ho$) and analyzes their evolution under local noise channels (amplitude damping) and local measurement protocols (LOCC).
key_observables: Binegativity ($N_2(ho)$), Negativity ($N(ho)$), and Concurrence ($C(v)$).
important_parameters: The damping probability ($\eta$) and a continuous parameter ($p$) used to construct the family of counterexamples.
main_assumptions: The counterexamples are constructed using specific state forms ($ho^*$) and the analysis of the probability-weighted average over measurement branches.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept and the conjecture, then presents a concrete counterexample using amplitude damping on a full-rank state. Subsequently, it analyzes a continuous family of counterexamples under a one-way LOCC protocol, demonstrating the increase in the averaged binegativity.
why_interesting: This work directly impacts the understanding of entanglement measures, which is fundamental to quantum information theory and the characterization of quantum resources in open quantum systems.
